title: Stage names a learner sees
statement: Whether showing learners an ability-stage name such as beginner leads them to act like beginners is unsettled and unchecked against the research on ability labelling.
example: One Grade 3 design asks this of a child told they are a beginner for sixteen units.
detail: A Grade 3 reading lesson design lists naming its stages as one thing to settle before it is built: beginner, intermediate and expert is the obvious set, but a child told they are a beginner for sixteen units may behave like one (`g9/sources/Readventure - Lesson Design and Scaffolding - Updated.docx`, lines 112-113). It asks for a look at the research on ability labelling before any name is put on screen.
against: A Grade 9 lesson design specification names its stages beginner, intermediate and expert without saying whether learners see the names (`g9/sources/Year 9 ELA_ Lesson Design Specification for Devfactory.md`, line 19).
